primitives.summary: Configures the SDK for one consumer/provider pair — the object every other primitive hangs off.

signature.name: consumer
signature.description: The consumer's name, as 'consumer-session/create' records it.

signature.name: options
signature.description: Where the contract is written (default: a 'contracts' directory under the working directory) and how the engine is reached (the embedding, spec.md §2; ADR 0003).

primitives.semantics: Makes no protocol call when constructed. The engine is started, and 'engine/hello' sent offering protocol version 1 (engine-protocol spec §5), when the first 'execute' needs it; one engine and at most one open consumer session belong to one configured object, and a test suite uses one configured object. A hello that fails, or agrees any protocol version other than 1, fails that first 'execute' with the engine's error; nothing is retried.

errors.surfaced-as: thrown from the first 'execute', carrying the engine's 'details.supported' verbatim

primitives.summary: Begins a new interaction specification.
primitives.semantics: Opens a new interaction-spec document (contract spec §1, schema contract.schema.json#/$defs/InteractionSpec) with 'description' set and 'transport' set to { kind: 'http', mode: 'passive' } — 'request' and 'response' describe an HTTP exchange the consumer initiates, which is exactly a passive HTTP interaction (engine-protocol spec §8.2). No protocol call happens; the document is submitted by 'execute'. The builder is opaque to the protocol and exists only in the idiomatic layer; building the same chain twice produces two equal documents.

primitives.summary: Declares a provider state this interaction requires.

signature.name: params
signature.description: Optional literal state parameters, a JSON object. Variant-bound parameters (variant semantics spec §6) are not yet part of this primitive.

primitives.semantics: Appends { name, params } to the interaction-spec document's 'states' array, in call order; 'params' is omitted from the entry when not given, never written as null or {}. Calling 'given' again appends a further state. 'params' is passed through as written — no key is renamed, reordered or coerced. Contributes nothing to the variant space.

primitives.summary: Declares the request part of an HTTP interaction.

signature.name: parts
signature.description: Any of method, path, query, headers and body.

primitives.semantics: Populates 'parts.request', one slot per member given; a member not given produces no slot. 'method', 'path' and 'body' are compiled by the 'literal' rules (this document) — a bare value becomes an 'equality' node, a shape helper is used as authored — and are otherwise untouched: the method is not upper-cased and the path is not normalised, because repairing a value is the engine's call to reject, not the SDK's to make (SDK spec §2.1). 'query' and 'headers' are each a map of name to value and compile to an 'object' node with one member per name, because the HTTP transport carries each as a map of name to a list of values (shape spec §3.6): a string value becomes an 'equality' node over the one-element list [value]; a list becomes an 'equality' node over that list, each element written by the same rule; a shape helper describes the one value and becomes an 'each-like' node whose 'items' is that shape, with 'min' 1 and 'max' 1 — exactly one value, matching it. The bounds are written because an unbounded 'each-like' contributes a cardinality dimension (shape spec §6.4), which on the request side would require the consumer to send the header twice in some variant; bounded at one, the dimension has a single point and contributes nothing. Several values each matching a shape are not expressible through this rule. A value that is not a string is written as the one string that spells it, but only where every language spells it the same way: a whole number whose magnitude is at most 2^53 - 1 becomes its shortest decimal form (no exponent, no trailing zeros, no leading '+', so 3 and 3.0 are the same value and both are written '3'), and a boolean becomes 'true' or 'false'. Every other value is refused at the call, before any document is built — a number with a fractional part or a larger magnitude, a date or a time, null, a map, a list holding any of these — because a value whose spelling differs by language ('1.5e3' or '1500.0'; '1e+21' or '1.0E21') would make two SDKs send different bytes for the same test, and a date has no format the SDK may choose (compare 'datetime', this document). This is not the coercion 'method' and 'path' forbid: those are values the engine judges as the author wrote them, while a header or query value reaches the transport as a string and nothing else (shape spec §3.6), which is why this rule already writes a bare string as a one-element list. Header names are lower-cased, which is the only spelling the HTTP transport presents them under, since HTTP header names are case-insensitive; query names are kept exactly as written, since they are not. Two header names that are the same once lower-cased are refused at the call, for the reason 'regex' refuses a flag it cannot carry (this document): the SDK made the collision by lower-casing, the engine never sees the declaration that would be dropped, and an author who means one header with two values writes the list form.

errors.surfaced-as: thrown from 'execute' (this primitive makes no call), with the engine's 'problems' — each a 'pointer' into the interaction-spec document and a 'message' — carried verbatim

primitives.summary: Declares the response part of an HTTP interaction.

signature.name: parts
signature.description: Any of status, headers and body.

primitives.semantics: Identical treatment to 'request' (this document), populating 'parts.response': 'status' and 'body' by the 'literal' rules, 'headers' by the name-to-list rule with names lower-cased.

primitives.summary: Submits an interaction and runs the test closure once per variant the engine selects.

signature.name: interaction
signature.description: A built interaction ('interaction' and its chain).

signature.name: closure
signature.description: Runs once per selected variant, receiving (mock, variant).

primitives.semantics: In order: 'create' with the configured consumer and provider, if this configured object has no open session yet (one session per suite — sessions amortise state and transport setup, and 'finalise' writes all of a suite's interactions into one contract); 'add-interaction' with the built document; 'start-transport' with transport 'http', if the session has not started one; 'variants' for the returned handle. Then, for each variant in the order 'variants' returned them: 'serve-variant' with that variant's 'id', then the closure with (mock, variant) — 'mock' exposes the transport's 'endpoint' descriptor and, for HTTP, its 'base-url' as 'mock.url'; 'variant' is the descriptor exactly as 'variants' returned it (id and label — variant semantics spec §2.2; assignment and origin — §3.9). The closure runs once per selected variant, never once per declared variant, and never zero times: a one-variant selection still runs it once. A closure that throws or rejects fails that variant only: every remaining variant still runs, and 'execute' then fails once, naming every failed variant by label and id with its cause. An engine error is not a closure's verdict and is not recorded as one: when any operation 'execute' sends answers with an error — including a 'serve-variant' inside the loop — 'execute' fails at once with that error, and the variants after it do not run. The guarantee above is about what a test decided; an engine that cannot arm this variant cannot arm the next one either, and one failure per remaining variant would say the tests failed when the engine did. 'execute' does not decide whether any variant passed from the values the mock saw — the engine's verdict on each exchange (a request that did not match, a variant never exercised) is returned by 'finalise', and 'finalise' fails on it (this document).

errors.surfaced-as: thrown before any variant runs, from 'add-interaction', 'problems' verbatim
thrown before any variant runs, from 'variants'
thrown from 'execute', like any engine error (this document). The SDK owns the session's lifetime end to end, so reaching a user means the engine lost the session — never something the caller did

primitives.summary: Ends the suite's session, and writes the contract if the engine produced one.
primitives.semantics: Sends 'finalise' for the open session, if there is one, and then ends the engine (engine-protocol spec §6 — for the subprocess embedding, closing its stdin). When the result carries 'contract' — present iff every interaction verified on every variant it required (engine-protocol spec §8.2) — writes it to '<contract directory>/<consumer>-<provider>.janus.json' (the '.janus.json' suffix is contract spec §2.3's convention; the '<consumer>-<provider>' stem is this primitive's) as compact UTF-8 JSON followed by one LF (contract spec §2.4), members in the order the engine returned them; the SDK never reorders, merges or edits a contract. When it does not, fails, naming every interaction and variant whose status is not 'verified' with the engine's mismatches, and writes nothing. It also writes nothing, and fails naming the interactions, when any 'execute' in the session failed — even though the engine returned a contract: the engine verified the exchanges, but only the closure knows whether the consumer handled what it was sent, and a contract must not claim a variant the consumer's own test failed on. (The protocol cannot yet tell the engine that a closure failed; until it can, this is the one verdict the SDK holds that the engine does not.) The test-framework integration MUST run 'finalise' after the suite's last 'execute', including when an 'execute' failed: sessions are the only resource (engine-protocol spec §7.1) and 'finalise' is the only way to release one. Calling it with no open session ends the engine and does nothing else.

primitives.summary: A plain value where a shape is expected — no helper call at all.
primitives.semantics: The rule every other primitive's 'nested-shape' parameter, and every member of a request or response part, is compiled by. A shape helper's result is used as authored. A string, number, boolean or null becomes an 'equality' node with the value as its example (shape spec §4.1). An object — a plain map written in the DSL, not a helper's result — becomes an 'object' node with one member per key, each compiled by this rule, in the order written (shape-language example order-payload.md §2); members the provider sends beyond these are admitted (shape spec §4.3). A list becomes an 'array' node with one positional entry per element, each compiled by this rule (shape spec §4.1). Nothing else is inferred: no value becomes a kind predicate, a regex or an optional without its helper. How the idiomatic layer tells a helper's result from a plain map that happens to have a 'shape' member is the style guide's business; it MUST NOT be by looking for a 'shape' member.

primitives.summary: Marks a body as a JSON document.
primitives.semantics: Compiles 'document' by the 'literal' rules and adds nothing: the HTTP transport writes a structured body through the engine's JSON content component and labels it application/json (design 2.6), so there is no node for 'json' to emit today. It exists because the RFC's DSL names the body's content type at the call site, and a later content type — or a per-slot content-type declaration in the interaction spec — will give it one; until then it is sugar, and a body written without it compiles identically.

primitives.summary: A whole-number value.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to an 'integer' kind predicate (shape spec §4.2) with 'example' as its example. Contributes no variant dimension.

primitives.summary: Any numeric value.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to a 'number' kind predicate (shape spec §4.2) with 'example' as its example. Contributes no variant dimension.

primitives.summary: A number written with a fractional part.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to a 'decimal' kind predicate (shape spec §4.2) with 'example' as its example. Where a content component cannot distinguish lexical forms this degrades to 'number' at the component boundary; the SDK still emits 'decimal'. Contributes no variant dimension.

primitives.summary: A string value.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to a 'string' kind predicate (shape spec §4.2) with 'example' as its example. Contributes no variant dimension.

primitives.summary: A boolean value.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to a 'boolean' kind predicate (shape spec §4.2) with 'example' as its example. Contributes no variant dimension.

primitives.summary: A string parsing as a datetime.

signature.name: format
signature.description: Optional, in shape spec §4.2's pattern language.

primitives.semantics: Compiles to a 'datetime' node (shape spec §4.2) with 'example' as its example and 'format' when given. When 'format' is not given the node has none — which means ISO-8601 (shape spec §4.2) — and the SDK does not infer one from the example.

primitives.summary: A string parsing as a calendar date.
primitives.semantics: Identical treatment to 'datetime' (this document), for the 'date' operator.

primitives.summary: A string parsing as a time of day.
primitives.semantics: Identical treatment to 'datetime' (this document), for the 'time' operator.

primitives.summary: A string matching a pattern.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to a 'regex' node with 'pattern' and 'example'. Matching is unanchored (shape spec §4.2), so the SDK MUST NOT anchor the pattern; an author who means a full match writes '^...$'. A pattern the language represents with out-of-band options — flags, modifiers — that the pattern text cannot carry is refused at the call, before any document is built: silently dropping an option would change what the pattern means.

primitives.summary: Enumerates the literal values a field may take.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to an 'any-of' node (shape spec §4.1, §5.3) with 'options' as its literal set, in the order given, and the first option as its example. Contributes one 'value' variant dimension, one point per option (shape spec §6.4) — computed by the engine, not the SDK.

primitives.summary: A discriminated union of alternatives.

signature.name: alternatives
signature.description: Name -> the alternative, a plain map binding 'discriminator' to a literal.

primitives.semantics: Compiles to a 'one-of' node with 'discriminator' and one alternative per name, in the order given, each compiled by the 'literal' rules — so the discriminator's literal becomes an 'equality' node like any other scalar. Adds no 'default': absent, the engine takes the lexicographically first alternative (shape spec §6.1). The SDK does not check that the alternatives bind distinct discriminator literals, or bind one at all: the engine rejects both with 'interaction-invalid' when the interaction is added (shape spec §5.4), and a second check here could only disagree with it. Contributes one 'alternative' variant dimension (shape spec §6.4).

errors.surfaced-as: thrown from 'execute', naming the duplicate or missing discriminator in the engine's own words

primitives.summary: Marks a value as may-be-absent.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to an 'optional' node (shape spec §4.4) wrapping 'of' compiled by the 'literal' rules, with no further transformation. Contributes one 'presence' variant dimension (shape spec §6.4).

primitives.summary: Marks a value as may-be-null.
primitives.semantics: Identical treatment to 'optional' (this document), for the 'nullable' operator (shape spec §4.4).

primitives.summary: Asserts that a member is absent.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to a 'forbidden' node (shape spec §4.4), which admits absence and nothing else. It takes no nested shape and no example — a constraint on a value that must not exist is not a thing to write — so the helper takes no arguments. Contributes no variant dimension: what it admits has one point, and only width earns a dimension (shape spec §6.1). The SDK does not check where it was written: a 'forbidden' node belongs in a slot and MUST NOT be wrapped by 'optional' or 'nullable' (shape spec §5.1, §5.2), and the engine rejects a misplaced one with 'interaction-invalid' when the interaction is added.

errors.surfaced-as: thrown from 'execute', naming the misplaced node in the engine's own words

primitives.summary: An array of like elements, with a cardinality.
primitives.semantics: Compiles to an 'each-like' node (shape spec §4.1) with 'items' compiled by the 'literal' rules, and 'min' and 'max' only when given — absent, 'min' means 1 and 'max' unbounded in the shape itself, so the SDK does not write the defaults. Contributes one 'cardinality' variant dimension (shape spec §6.4).
